.qc-cache/coldwater-2026-10-01-lifecycle-controls/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md: Known false positives / Likert versus weighted
evidence: Source-level check confirmed: Python -B/tomllib enumeration found 2 binary gate criteria, 79 binary Functional criteria, 6 binary Polish criteria and 6 five-point Likert Visual criteria. Every Likert description contains exactly the five nonempty integer anchors 1 through 5. In frozen task/tests/scored/visual/judge.toml:20-29, 35-44, 50-59, 65-74, 80-89 and 95-104, typography, colour, geometry, hierarchy, consistency and responsive composition retain graded craft anchors. task/tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:23,32,41,50,59,68 sets observable usability thresholds (reachable panes, named controls, keyboard reachability, visible focus, completed navigation and recognisable surfaces), not binary aesthetic excellence. Functional criteria are concrete execution/storage/editor outcomes; e.g. the monospaced-face and syntax-colouring presence checks do not grade font craft. This fits public ui.md:3-9. A plausible weak app with named/reachable controls but several mismatched font treatments can satisfy those binary thresholds while receiving typography anchor 3 rather than full visual credit; a dead Run cannot satisfy render/judge.toml:25. A conforming native-looking app with mobile tabs, native focus and simple styling is explicitly allowed by polish/judge.toml:23,50,59 and visual/judge.toml:40,55,85,99-100, so those alternatives do not falsely fail on style. The workbook Internal E42 historical no-Likert comment is superseded for this check by the frozen skill and quality-checks.md:170. Visual prompt:48-52 instructs integer 1-5 scores and full-credit clarity rather than aesthetic perfection. score.py:45-47 preserves weighted dimension values instead of reducing them to pass/fail; its SHA256 13de2b3885967e22aa13ded3bf33c354e3e741e85be871612c04e996eef5c04e exactly matches the frozen template. Current raw CLI admission evidence agrees with all five judge hashes/counts; cli-stdout.log SHA256 b1a2e30153bece78e3e5273e046713a2783183994a0093d40e3eac3954c8b38f and RESULTS.json SHA256 ee5d9be4bfd8106fc79d569ca52be7100d8af7fb5976df777ad3ef374a4389f8 were verified against the current index. Those records explicitly say judge_launched=false/provider_invoked=false. This Pass establishes type/anchor fit by inspected bytes, not configured judge behavior, empirical reward discrimination, an Oracle/model score or private deterministic-checker execution.
